f: Who was the first caliph after the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه, chosen in 11 AH (632 CE).

f: How long was Abu Bakr's رضي الله عنه caliphate?
b: About two years and three months, until his death in 13 AH (634 CE).

f: What were the Riddah wars?
b: Abu Bakr's رضي الله عنه campaigns against tribes who refused zakat or followed false prophets after the Prophet's ﷺ passing.

f: Under which caliph was the Qur'an first gathered into one written collection, and why?
b: Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه, after many memorisers were martyred at the Battle of Yamamah. Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه led the work.

f: Who was the second caliph?
b: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه, from 13 to 23 AH (634–644 CE).

f: Which great lands were opened in the time of 'Umar رضي الله عنه?
b: Iraq, Syria (al-Sham), Jerusalem, Egypt and most of Persia.

f: Which calendar did 'Umar رضي الله عنه establish?
b: The Hijri calendar, counted from the Prophet's ﷺ migration to Madinah.

f: Which title was 'Umar رضي الله عنه the first to be called?
b: Amir al-Mu'minin, Commander of the Believers.

f: Who was the third caliph?
b: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan رضي الله عنه, from 23 to 35 AH (644–656 CE).

f: What did 'Uthman رضي الله عنه do with the Qur'an?
b: He had standard copies (masahif) written from the collection of Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه and sent to the main cities, uniting the Muslims on one written text.

f: Who was the fourth caliph?
b: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه, from 35 to 40 AH (656–661 CE).

f: Which city did 'Ali رضي الله عنه make his capital?
b: Kufa in Iraq.

f: What did al-Hasan ibn 'Ali رضي الله عنهما do in 41 AH, called the Year of Unity?
b: He gave up the caliphate to Mu'awiyah رضي الله عنه to end the fighting, as the Prophet ﷺ had foretold he would make peace between two great groups of Muslims.

f: Who founded the Umayyad caliphate, and where was its capital?
b: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan رضي الله عنه; its capital was Damascus.

f: Which Umayyad caliph built the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem?
b: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, completed around 72 AH (691–692 CE).

f: What change to coins and government did 'Abd al-Malik make?
b: He minted the first purely Islamic coins and made Arabic the language of government.

f: Which Umayyad caliph is famous for his justice and is often called the fifth rightly guided caliph?
b: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz رحمه الله (ruled 99–101 AH).

f: What did 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz رحمه الله order to preserve the Sunnah?
b: That the hadith be gathered and written down, fearing that knowledge would be lost with the passing of the scholars.

f: Who led the Muslim crossing into Spain (al-Andalus) in 92 AH (711 CE)?
b: Tariq ibn Ziyad, under Musa ibn Nusayr.

f: Which young commander opened Sind in the Indian subcontinent?
b: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Thaqafi, around 92 AH (711 CE).

f: When did the Abbasids take the caliphate from the Umayyads?
Which city did the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur build as his capital?
b: Baghdad, founded around 145 AH (762 CE).

f: What was the Bayt al-Hikmah (House of Wisdom)?
b: A great library and centre of learning and translation in Baghdad, which flourished under al-Ma'mun.

f: Which Abbasid caliph was known for his hajj and campaigns, and whose reign is remembered as a golden age?
b: Harun al-Rashid (ruled 170–193 AH).

f: What was the Mihnah?
b: The inquisition begun under al-Ma'mun to force scholars to say the Qur'an is created. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal رحمه الله stood firm and was imprisoned and flogged.

f: Which caliph ended the Mihnah?
b: al-Mutawakkil, around 234 AH (848 CE).

f: When did Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله live, and where?
b: 80–150 AH, in Kufa.

f: Who were the two most famous students of Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله?
b: Imam Abu Yusuf and Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani رحمهما الله.

f: Which post did Imam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله hold under Harun al-Rashid?
b: Chief judge (qadi al-qudat), the first to hold that title.

f: When did Imam Malik رحمه الله live, and what is his famous book?
b: 93–179 AH in Madinah; his book is al-Muwatta'.

f: When did Imam al-Shafi'i رحمه الله live, and what is he known for in usul?
b: 150–204 AH; his al-Risalah is the first written book of usul al-fiqh.

f: When did Imam al-Bukhari رحمه الله die?
Who are the two imams of Sunni creed after whom the Ash'ari and Maturidi schools are named?
b: Imam Abu'l-Hasan al-Ash'ari (d. 324 AH) and Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi (d. 333 AH) رحمهما الله.

f: Which great teacher of the Nizamiyyah in Baghdad wrote Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din?
b: Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali رحمه الله (d. 505 AH).

f: Who founded the Qadiri path of tasawwuf in Baghdad?
b: Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani رحمه الله (d. 561 AH).

f: Which Umayyad prince escaped the Abbasids and founded a state in al-Andalus?
b: 'Abd al-Rahman I (al-Dakhil), in 138 AH (756 CE), with his capital at Cordoba.

f: Which ruler of al-Andalus declared himself caliph in 316 AH (929 CE)?
b: 'Abd al-Rahman III.

f: What was the last Muslim kingdom in al-Andalus, and when did it fall?
b: Granada, in 897 AH (1492 CE).

f: When did the Crusaders take Jerusalem?
Which ruler united Syria and began the struggle against the Crusaders before Salah al-Din?
b: Nur al-Din Zangi رحمه الله (d. 569 AH).

f: At which battle did Salah al-Din رحمه الله defeat the Crusaders in 583 AH (1187 CE)?
b: The Battle of Hattin, after which he retook Jerusalem.

f: How did Salah al-Din رحمه الله treat the people of Jerusalem when he retook it?
b: With mercy: he let them leave in safety, unlike the massacre when the Crusaders had taken it.

f: When did the Mongols sack Baghdad and end the Abbasid caliphate there?
b: 656 AH (1258 CE), under Hulagu.

f: At which battle did the Mamluks stop the Mongol advance in 658 AH (1260 CE)?
b: The Battle of 'Ayn Jalut in Palestine, under Sultan Qutuz and Baybars.

f: Who founded the Ottoman state?
b: 'Uthman (Osman) I, around 699 AH (1299 CE).

f: Who opened Constantinople, and when?
b: Sultan Muhammad (Mehmed) al-Fatih, in 857 AH (1453 CE).

f: Which hadith did Muslims see fulfilled in the opening of Constantinople?
b: 'Constantinople will be opened; how excellent its commander and how excellent that army.' (Ahmad)

f: Which Ottoman sultan is known as the Lawgiver (al-Qanuni)?
b: Sulayman the Magnificent (ruled 926–974 AH, 1520–1566 CE).

f: When was the Ottoman caliphate formally abolished?
Which Mughal emperor, known for his piety, ordered the compiling of al-Fatawa al-'Alamgiriyyah?
b: Aurangzeb 'Alamgir رحمه الله (ruled 1068–1118 AH).

f: What is al-Fatawa al-Hindiyyah (al-'Alamgiriyyah)?
b: A great collection of Hanafi rulings compiled by a council of scholars in India.

f: Which great scholar of Delhi wrote Hujjat Allah al-Balighah?
b: Shah Wali Allah al-Dihlawi رحمه الله (d. 1176 AH).
